subject: math
title: 2D Shapes and 3D Objects: Name, Sort and Compare
seo_title: Grade 1 Math 2D Shapes and 3D Objects Worksheets (BC Curriculum, Free, Answer Key)
meta_desc: Free Grade 1 math worksheets on 2D shapes and 3D objects for the BC curriculum: name circles, triangles, squares, rectangles and hexagons, sort shapes by sides and corners, name cubes, spheres, cones and cylinders, tell flat from solid and trace flat faces. 100 questions with an answer key.
key_big: 2D shapes are flat. 3D objects are solid. Turning a shape never changes its name.
key_sub: Count sides and corners to name a 2D shape. A square on its corner is still a square. A ball is a sphere, not a circle. Trace a flat face of a 3D object to get a 2D shape.

faq.q: What shapes do Grade 1 students learn in BC math?
faq.a: In Geometry and measurement, Grade 1 students compare 2D shapes and 3D objects. They name circles, triangles, squares, rectangles and hexagons, sort shapes by sides and corners, and name cubes, spheres, cones and cylinders.

faq.q: What is the difference between a 2D shape and a 3D object?
faq.a: A 2D shape is flat, like a drawing on paper. A 3D object is solid and you can hold it, like a ball (a sphere) or a can (a cylinder).

faq.q: Is a square turned on its corner still a square?
faq.a: Yes. It still has 4 sides of the same length, so it is a square. Many children call it a “diamond”, but turning a shape never changes its name.

faq.q: How can I help my Grade 1 child learn shapes at home?
faq.a: Go on a shape hunt: find a ball (sphere), a can (cylinder), a number cube (cube) and an ice-cream cone (cone). Trace their flat faces on paper and sort the drawings by sides and corners.

sets.title: Sort shapes by sides and corners

items.q: Mateo uses the same 2 groups. Where does a circle go?
items.e: A circle has no straight sides. It does not go in either group.

items.q: Liam sorts shapes into 2 groups. Where does a hexagon go?
items.e: A hexagon has 6 corners. It goes in the corners group.

items.q: Which shape is the odd one out?
items.e: C is round. It has no corners. The others have 6 corners. They are hexagons.

items.q: How many corners does a circle have?
items.e: A circle is round all the way. It has no corners: 0.

items.q: How many triangles can you see?
items.e: Look for 3 sides. There are 3 triangles. The turned one and the thin one count too.

items.q: How many corners does this shape have?

items.q: These are in one group. What is the sorting rule?
items.e: The sizes and colours are different. Count the sides of each one: 6. The rule is 6 sides.

items.q: Which shape is NOT a triangle?

items.q: These are in one group. What is the sorting rule?

items.q: How many squares can you see?

sets.title: Faces you can trace: word problems

items.e: The bottom of the can is a flat circle. Lucas draws a circle.
